Attachments.Name: Proposed Int. No. 891-A Fiscal Impact Statement - City Council

Summary: This bill would prohibit any entity or service provider from engaging in surveillance pricing, defined as pricing set completely or in part by algorithm that uses personal data to offer different prices to different customers for the same goods or services. This bill would permit the use of bona fide discounts. This bill would exempt certain regulated activity. This bill would provide for enforcement by the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP). Entities and service providers in violation of this law would be subject to civil penalties of no more than $1,000 for each violation.

Proposed Int. No. 891-A

By The Speaker (Council Member Menin) and Council Members Hanif, Louis, Narcisse, Restler, Hudson, Epstein, Wilson, Brewer, Maloney, Schulman, Banks, Santosuosso, Stevens, J. Sanchez, Hanks, Aldebol, Gutiérrez and the Public Advocate (Mr. Williams)

A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting surveillance pricing 

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subchapter 2 of chapter 5 of title 20 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 20-709.1 to read as follows: 
§ 20-709.1 Surveillance pricing prohibited. a. Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Algorithm. The term “algorithm” means a computational process or system that applies one or more sets of rules, including rules generated by a natural person or by a computation process or system, to generate outputs based on inputs and/or to define a sequence of operations.
Bona fide discount. The term “bona fide discount” means a genuine reduction in price that is referred to as such to consumers, including generally available reductions in price from the reference price based on bulk purchases or subscriptions. Entities and service providers may reasonably interpret the term “bona fide discount” to mean a genuine reduction from a contemporaneous or recent reference price that is established absent of unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices as required by section 349 of the general business law. A bona fide discount may include, but is not limited to, clearly and conspicuously posted promotional periods, end-of-season sales, flash sales, early-bird sales, inventory-based pricing, price matching policies, and rebates, to the extent that such discount is generally available without the utilization of personal data.
Bona fide custom discount. The term “bona fide custom discount” means a bona fide discount consistent with federal, state, and local anti-discrimination laws offered:
1. By an entity to a consumer who affirmatively and knowingly enrolls in a loyalty, membership or rewards program, including but not limited to signing up for a mailing list, registering for promotional communication, or participating in a promotional event, provided the discount is offered and clearly and conspicuously disclosed to all members in a given local geographic market, or commonly used distribution channels of such loyalty program pursuant to publicly disclosed terms and conditions. Such loyalty, membership or rewards programs may include tiers of bona fide discounts based on prior purchase history data provided that the tiers are clearly and conspicuously disclosed and that such prior purchase history data is not paired, combined, or cross-referenced with any other personal data except enrollment in the loyalty, membership, or rewards program.
2. By an entity to a consumer based on such consumer’s voluntary self-identification with a broadly defined class of consumers including, but not limited to, military veterans, active duty personnel, seniors, teachers, or employees, or individuals belonging to a class of consumers based on date of birth or anniversary of membership in a loyalty program, based on information provided affirmatively and knowingly by the consumer and not derived or inferred by the entity from any other data, provided the basis of the discount is clearly and conspicuously disclosed to all members of the defined class of consumers.
3. By an entity, except when acting as an operator of an online marketplace, to a consumer based solely on such consumer’s prior purchase history, including goods or services purchased, timing or frequency of purchases including first time or subsequent purchases, returns or cancellations, with such specific entity, provided that:
(a) such prior purchase history data is not paired, combined, or cross-referenced with any other consumer data except the fact of enrollment in a loyalty, membership, or rewards program; and
(b) the entity clearly and conspicuously discloses its use of prior purchase history data.
4. By the operator of an online marketplace, provided the online marketplace clearly and conspicuously discloses its use of prior purchase history data:
(a) based solely on a consumer’s prior purchase history, including goods or services purchased, timing or frequency of purchases including first-time or subsequent purchases, returns or cancellations with the same independent third-party entity offering the good or service to which the bona fide discount is applied, provided that such prior purchase history data is not paired, combined, or cross-referenced with any other personal data, including but not limited to data held by such operator of such online marketplace related to any other independent third-party entities, and such operator’s own transaction data where such operator also offers goods and services; or
(b) based on a consumer’s prior purchase history, including goods or services purchased, timing or frequency of purchases including first-time purchase, returns or cancellations, collected through the online marketplace to offer a one-time discount from the reference price to new customers of a particular independent, third-party entity on that online marketplace, provided the consumer’s prior purchase history data is not used to set or change the reference price for any goods or services to which the discount may be applied.
(c) based solely on a consumer’s prior purchase history including goods or services purchased, timing or frequency of purchases including first-time purchase, returns or cancellations, collected through the online marketplace to offer a discount on the fees associated with the delivery or fulfillment of orders places through such online marketplace, provided the consumer’s prior purchase history data is not used to set or change the reference price for any goods or services to which a discount may apply.
5. Bona fide custom discount does not include any reduction in reference price based on personal data other than personal data identified in paragraphs 1 through 4 of this definition. 
(a) Nothing herein shall prevent an entity from notifying the consumer of a bona fide custom discount or automatically applying a bona fide custom discount where the entity has knowledge of the consumer’s eligibility for such a discount, provided that entity does not change the reference price. Where an entity provides a bona fide custom discount automatically, such entity shall notify the consumer of their eligibility.
(b) Nothing herein shall prevent an entity from marketing a bona fide discount to a consumer for the purposes of attracting a new customer or reengaging a consumer as a customer with the entity unless such consumer has opted out of such communications. 
Consumer. The term “consumer” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision d of section 20-701.
Consumer price. The term “consumer price” means the reference price with adjustments based on bona fide discounts, including sales, coupons, promotions, or other discounts except bona fide custom discounts. 
Covered business.  The term “covered business” shall mean any single entity or any entity that is part of a chain with fewer than 15 locations nationally doing business under the same name and offering for sale substantially the same goods or services and which conducts a majority of its business from a physical location or locations in New York city. 
Entity. The term “entity” means any natural person, firm, organization, partnership, association, corporation, or any other entity domiciled or transacting with consumers in the city. 
Independent third-party entity. The term “independent third-party entity” means any entity that engages in the sale, purchase, payment, storage, shipping, or delivery of goods or services to a consumer in the city through an online marketplace. 
Online marketplace. The term “online marketplace” means an entity that operates a public or semi-public website, online service, online application, mobile application or other electronically based or accessed platform through which a consumer in the city engages in the sale, purchase, payment, storage, shipping, or delivery of a good or service that allows for, facilitates, or enables independent, third-party entities to engage in the sale, purchase, payment, storage, shipping, or delivery of a good or service to a consumer in the city. Such term shall not include a “high-volume for-hire vehicle service” as defined in subdivision gg of section 19-502. 
Personal data. The term “personal data” means any data that identifies or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a specific consumer or device. Personal data does not include location data that is affirmatively and knowingly provided or shared by a consumer and used:
(a) for the purpose of calculating trip duration and mileage costs associated with location-based service, such as transportation, delivery, and courier logistics; 
(b) to assess current or historical local supply and demand conditions; or
(c) for the purpose of aggregating local marketplace conditions.
Reference price. The term “reference price” means the actual amount a consumer is required to pay for any good or service, including mandatory fees or charges necessary to receive such good or service except taxes or fees imposed by a government, that is openly and actively offered to the public in regular course of business for a reasonably substantial and recent period of time. 
Service provider. The term “service provider” means any entity that acts on behalf of another entity that is subject to this section. 
Surveillance pricing. The term “surveillance pricing” means pricing set completely or in part by an algorithm that uses personal data to offer different prices to different customers for the same goods or services and does not include bona fide custom discounts. Notwithstanding this definition, the term “surveillance pricing” shall not include prices, fees, or discounts offered by a securities broker-dealer or registered investment adviser based on assets under management, account characteristics, or the customer relationship including the linking of relationships together for pricing.
b. Prohibition on certain pricing practices. 1. No service provider or other entity shall set or adjust the reference price or consumer price of a good or service using surveillance pricing to a consumer. Nothing in this section shall be interpreted to affect prices or discounts except to prohibit surveillance pricing. 
2. No service provider or other entity shall advertise, promote, label, or publish a statement, display, image, offer or announcement using surveillance pricing to a consumer.
3. No service provider or other entity shall collect, use, sell, retain, share for valuable consideration, or disclose personal data for the purpose of facilitating surveillance pricing to the consumer.
4. No service provider or other entity shall offer a bona fide custom discount unless such discount is offered uniformly to any consumer who meets the disclosed eligibility conditions or criteria. 
c. Publication of procedures; records. 1. A service provider or other entity that uses surveillance pricing or offers a bona fide custom discount shall develop and maintain reasonable procedures for consumers to request and receive information regarding what personal data is considered and how the personal data was considered when setting particular prices. 
2. Such procedures required to be maintained by this subdivision, and all personal data referenced in such procedures, including but not limited to all such personal data used for surveillance pricing or offering a bona fide custom discount, shall be made available to the department electronically upon request, consistent with applicable laws and in accordance with rules promulgated hereunder and with reasonable notice.
d. Exceptions. Nothing in this section shall apply to:
1. A person who is subject to the insurance law or regulations promulgated thereunder.
2. A service provider’s or other entity’s use of personal data to set or adjust the price or terms of a good or service based in whole or in part on an evaluation of creditworthiness, including the pricing of credit, extension or granting of credit, or the refusal to extend based on data provided in a consumer report as defined by the fair credit reporting act, section 1681 of title 15 of the United States code.
3. Pricing required or expressly authorized by federal or state law.
4. A service provider acting on behalf of an entity subject to this section, unless the service provider shows reckless disregard of the entity’s conduct relating to pricing that is prohibited by this section.
e. Enforcement and Penalties. 1. Any person who violates this section shall be subject to a civil penalty of no more than $1,000 for each violation. A violation of any provision of this section shall constitute a separate violation with respect to each consumer or transaction. 
2. In a proceeding alleging a violation of this section at a tribunal established within the office of administrative trials and hearings or within any agency of the city designated to conduct such a proceeding, the department may seek an order imposing all applicable civil penalties authorized pursuant to this section or as otherwise authorized by law, and actual damages sustained by consumers. 
3. Whenever a person has engaged in any act or practice which constitutes a violation of any provision of this section or of any rule promulgated thereunder, the city may make application to the supreme court by action, proceeding, or special proceeding. An application to the supreme court made pursuant to this section may seek an order:
(a) enjoining such acts or practices, including by granting a temporary or permanent injunction or a restraining order;
(b) imposing civil penalties pursuant to this section;
(c) compelling a defendant to make restitution of all monies, property, or other things of value, or proceeds thereof, received directly or indirectly as a result of any such violation;
(d) directing that the amount of money or the property or other things of value recovered be paid into an account established pursuant to section 2601 of the New York civil practice law and rules from which shall be paid over to any and all consumers who purchased the goods or services during the period of violation such sum as was paid by such consumer in a transaction involving the prohibited acts or practices, plus any costs incurred by such claimants in making and pursuing their complaints; provided that if such claims exceed the sum recovered into the account, the awards to consumers shall be prorated according to the value of each claim proved;
(e) directing a defendant to pay to the city the costs and disbursements of the action or proceeding and the costs of the city’s investigation leading to the judgment; or if not recovered from a defendant, such costs are to be deducted by the city from the grand recovery before distribution to the consumers;
(f) directing that any money, property, or other things of value in the account described in this subdivision and unclaimed by any consumer with such claims within six years from creation of the account, be paid to the city; and
(g) granting all other appropriate relief.
4. In addition to the authority granted to the department under section 2203 of the charter, the corporation counsel may initiate any investigation to ascertain such facts as may be necessary for the commencement of an action or proceeding pursuant to this section, and in connection therewith shall have the power to issue subpoenas to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of documents, to administer oaths and to examine such persons as are deemed necessary.
5. Corrective action request. Notwithstanding any inconsistent provision of this subdivision, if the department finds that any covered business has violated this subchapter for the first time, the department shall notify such covered business of such violation before bringing any proceeding alleging such violation. Such covered business may submit to the department within 30 days of receiving such notification evidence that the covered business has corrected the violation, including evidence that such covered business has provided restitution of all monies, property, or other things of value, or proceeds thereof, received directly or indirectly, as a result of any such violation, to any consumers harmed by the violation.  Nothing in this subdivision prohibits the department from bringing a proceeding for any such violation that has not been corrected within such 30 days. A violation shall not be considered corrected if such covered business has not provided restitution of all monies, property, or other things of value, or proceeds thereof, received directly or indirectly, as a result of any such violation, to any consumers harmed by the violation. Nothing in this subdivision prohibits the department from alleging additional violations discovered by the department after sending the notification required by this subdivision. 
f. Permitted practices. The provisions of this subchapter, and any rule promulgated thereunder, shall be enforced only where such enforcement is consistent with state and federal law. 
§ 2. This local law takes effect 1 year after it becomes law.
